title: Dynamics 365 Business Impact: How Small Architecture Changes Collapse Cycle Time and Turn Work into Progress

quotes.text: The thing most people miss, scale is a behavior, not a feature. If the system requires meetings to interpret every status, you've built ceremony, not acceleration.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sharp reframing of scaling a business application as behavior rather than features.

quotes.text: We implemented dynamics is not an outcome. It's a milestone on the way to an outcome. The outcome is speed. How fast your system turns work into progress.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core thesis that go-live is a milestone, not the result.

quotes.text: The rule is, brains in house hands near shore, strategy, priorities, and acceptance stay with your product owner.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable rule for splitting control and capacity in a nearshore model.

quotes.text: Adoption isn't training. It's the feeling that the system helps you win today. The pattern that works is rhythm, not rollouts.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear definition of adoption as everyday value instead of training events.

quotes.text: Agile here is not stand-ups with slide decks. It's shipping tiny testable changes tied to a metric.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise practical definition of agile delivery tied to measurable outcomes.

What 90 days of scaling looks like

takeaways: Go-live is only a milestone; the real outcome of Dynamics 365 is how fast the system turns work into progress.
Trim business process flows to a few stages with verb-based exit criteria and a handful of required fields, and automate handoffs on save.
Run Dynamics like a product with a single accountable product owner, a friction-focused backlog and a monthly release rhythm tied to metrics.
hook: Many Dynamics 365 implementations end up as digital filing cabinets that store activity instead of driving progress. This episode shows business application owners and CRM teams how small changes to stages, fields and handoffs, plus a product mindset with a steady release rhythm, collapse cycle time and lift every downstream metric.
